per_window.ps-ns: dynamic_in_window only for the unstructured C-terminal tail of the isolated apo PDZ; the core, including α5, is rigid at 298 K (average S2 0.9 ± 0.1, hetNOE about 0.8; J5, r4). Full-length S306A: no extra PDZ flexibility in the hexamer-rich apo sample at 50 °C (J14, r13) and partial PDZ decoupling with activator at 313 K (J15, r11), both inference only. Methyl S2axis·τc of the isolated PDZ (Fig. 2d,e of the 2024 paper) has no evidence row.
per_window.us-ms: dynamic_in_window: isolated apo PDZ in PBS pH 7.4 exchanges in the N-terminus, α5 and the α5-β15 loop, and α7 with its preceding loop; one global two-site fit per temperature gives τex 0.42 ± 0.004 ms, 15.2% minor at 298 K and 0.98 ± 0.005 ms, 16.1% at 283 K, where α7 and β17-β18 also exchange (J1 298 K, r1; J28 283 K, r2; derived kex about 2,400 and 1,020 s-1; per-residue ΔR2eff in Source Data sheet 2a localizes 30 residues at 298 K and 35 at 283 K under a ≥ 2 s-1 transcription rule); dimerization (KD ≥ 13 mM, at most about 7% of protomers) cannot explain the minor state. Methyl MQ CPMG gives τex 1.19 ± 0.07 ms, 16.6 ± 0.4% (J3, r3); R2β and model-free Rex agree (J4, r4). Full-length S306A constructs show exchange at α5 (J11, r10), a PDZ hexamer-interface contribution (J12, r14) and interface exchange enhanced by open neighbours (J13, r15), all inference_from_mutant. Peptide-bound isolated PDZ is not_measured (J8); the Ca2+/Zn2+ methyl CPMG in the source has no row (J9, search_insufficient).
per_window.slower_than_ms: not_measured for the isolated apo PDZ (J10). Trimer-hexamer interconversion of full-length S306A (koff 9.0 ± 1.1 s-1, 40 °C; J16, r12) and the isolated-PDZ ligand off-rates (J10 reason) are binding kinetics and are not counted.
per_window.undetermined: β14/β15 broadening of the isolated PDZ is unresolved between amide solvent exchange and conformational exchange (J6, r5). Full-length constructs: slow C/OI/OA state switching with client (J17, r17), PRE opening with Ca2+ or activator (J18-J20, r7-r9), Y361W fluorescence (J27, r29), crystal comparisons (J21, r31; J22, r28, structure_only) and MD (J23, r26, r27; J25, r22, r23; md_only). Not judged: the Cu2+ attenuation (r6), which the authors use as a solvent-exposure probe, not a dynamics measurement; protease-domain active-site rows outside the entry (r18, r19, r20, r24, r25, r30); the viscosity activity assay that names no coordinate (r21); the S276C state-population titration with an out-of-entry probe (r16); abstract-only rows r32-r40.

protein_summary.wt_apo_answer: Yes: the isolated apo PDZ (PBS pH 7.4) exchanges on the microsecond-millisecond scale in the N-terminus, helix α5 with its loop to β15, and α7 with its preceding loop, fit globally to one two-site process with τex 0.42 ± 0.004 ms (derived kex about 2,400 s-1) and a 15.2% minor state at 298 K, and 0.98 ± 0.005 ms (about 1,020 s-1) with 16.1% at 283 K, where α7 and the β17-β18 loop join; per-residue ΔR2eff in the Source Data (sheet 2a) places exchange on 30 residues at 298 K and 35 at 283 K under a ≥ 2 s-1 transcription rule, the fitted residue set itself is not listed, and the minor state is not identified, but it is not explained by dimerization.
open_conflicts: Backbone versus methyl lifetime at 298 K: 15N CPMG gives τex 0.42 ± 0.004 ms (15.2%, r1) while methyl MQ CPMG gives 1.19 ± 0.07 ms (16.6 ± 0.4%, r3); the authors call it one underlying process, but the samples differ (protonated in H2O versus deuterated ALVIT in 99.9% D2O) and the lifetimes differ about three-fold.

The 298 K and 283 K global fits use different residue sets: Source Data sheet 2a has ΔR2eff for 37 residues at 298 K and 50 at 283 K, and the exchanging sets differ (J1, J28); the residues entering each global fit are still not listed (r1, r2).
questions_for_gina: Which sample produced the RelaxDB HTPDZ_CPMG labels: 15N CPMG at 298 K or 283 K (700/900 MHz), and which construct (entry 352-458 plus LE, paper construct 349-458, BMRB 51320 entity of 156 residues)?

All isolated-PDZ NMR was in PBS pH 7.4 with no phosphate-free control, and the exchanging α5-β15 and pre-α7 loops are where divalent cations bind; should the exchange be flagged as untested for phosphate binding?
protein_summary.buffer_note: Untested condition, not a suspected artefact: every isolated-PDZ NMR measurement in the rows (r1-r6) used PBS pH 7.4, the methyl sample (r3) in 99.9% D2O, and the 2024 paper reports no phosphate-free NMR control; HEPES-buffered saline was used only for SEC-MALS with divalent metals. The source places divalent-cation binding (Ca2+ KD 4.1 mM, Zn2+ 1.6 mM) in the α5-β15 loop and the loop before α7, the same regions that exchange, so an anion-binding contribution is neither shown nor excluded. Full-length rows used Tris pH 8 (r7-r9) or a low-salt buffer whose composition is in an unread SI (r12-r15, r17).
